questions.stem: Why is Data Visualisation said to determine the success or failure of a data project?
options: Because it is the most expensive part of the project
Because it is what end users actually see; if they cannot make use of the data, all the other effort is wasted
Because it replaces the need for a data warehouse
Because regulators only audit dashboards
Because it is the first step of any data pipeline
questions.explanation: Data Visualisation is what is seen by end users; if they cannot see or use the implementation for decision support, the millions spent on strategy and warehouses are a waste of time and dollars.

questions.stem: Which phrase is quoted in I Am Datapedia! to capture the importance of Data Visualisation?
options: If you can't measure it, you can't manage it
Garbage in, garbage out
A picture is worth a thousand rows
If you can't draw it, you don't know it
Data is the new oil
questions.explanation: The author quotes the phrase 'If you can't draw it, you don't know it' and says it is very true.

questions.stem: What is the maximum number of KPIs recommended on one page of a dashboard?
options: Five
Two
Ten
Three
Twenty
questions.explanation: Rule 2 for good Data Visualisation is not to have more than five KPIs on one page.

questions.stem: Why must a dashboard builder know the cardinality of every table they are going to join?
options: To choose the right colour palette
To reduce licence costs
To eliminate the chance of producing Cartesian data
To satisfy the five-KPI rule
To decide which visualisation tool to buy
questions.explanation: Rule 3, flagged as very important, is that the user must know the cardinality of all tables being joined to eliminate the chance of Cartesian data.

questions.stem: How many tabular sections are recommended on a single dashboard page?
options: None; tables should never appear on dashboards
As many as fit on the screen
Exactly five
At least three
One, with a maximum of two
questions.explanation: Rule 4 is to use one tabular section on one page, going up to a maximum of two.

questions.stem: Where should data preparation, such as creating a third column by multiplying two others, be done according to the Data Visualisation rules?
options: In the visualisation tool, to save storage
In a spreadsheet exported from the dashboard
At the datastore level, even at the cost of extra storage, so the tool's memory is kept for slicing, dicing and drilling
In the end user's browser
It should not be done at all
questions.explanation: Rule 5 says never enrich or prepare data in the visualisation tool because it uses a lot of memory; do it at the datastore level, because the target is faster visualisation rather than saving storage.

questions.stem: How should the five Data Visualisation rules be treated?
options: As not hard rules; they can be optimised based on the infrastructure in place and are only a few of many
As mandatory rules that must never be varied
As rules that apply only to Tableau
As rules that apply only to BI Specialists
As legal requirements for dashboards
questions.explanation: The author notes these are not hard rules, can be optimised for the infrastructure in place, and are only a few of the many rules for an effective dashboard or report.

questions.stem: What big mistake are organisations described as making with regard to roles in Data Visualisation?
options: Hiring too many BI Specialists
Buying more than one visualisation tool
Letting end users build their own dashboards
Having their Data Analysts also perform BI Specialist roles, although these are different roles needing different tools
Storing dashboards in a Data Lake
questions.explanation: A big mistake is to have Data Analysts do BI Specialist roles as well; they are different roles and need different kinds of Data Visualisation tools.

questions.stem: In the author's own assessment, which tools are data analysis tools for Data Analysts, and which are for BI Specialists?
options: Cognos, OBIEE and SSRS for Data Analysts; Tableau, Qlik and Power BI for BI Specialists
Tableau, Qlik and Power BI for Data Analysts; Cognos, OBIEE and SSRS for BI Specialists
All six tools are for Data Analysts only
All six tools are for BI Specialists only
Excel for Data Analysts; everything else for BI Specialists
questions.explanation: In the author's assessment, Tableau, Qlik and Power BI are data analysis tools for Data Analysts, whereas Cognos, OBIEE and SSRS are for BI Specialists.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated rules for good Data Visualisation?
options: First identify all the relevant KPIs to be presented on the same page
Do not have more than five KPIs on one page
Know the cardinality of all tables to be joined
Never enrich or prepare data in the visualisation tool
Always prepare derived columns inside the visualisation tool to save storage
questions.explanation: Preparing data inside the visualisation tool is exactly what Rule 5 warns against; derived columns belong at the datastore level.
